rows.name: Adenosine
rows.dose: 6 mg (2 mL); deliver over 5 s for the modeled rapid push
rows.watch: Flush when required. Not for AFib, VT or a fast sinus rate.

rows.name: Amiodarone
rows.use: VF / pulseless VT support; AFib RVR, AT or SVT
rows.watch: Fast delivery lowers BP. Cumulative ≥2.2 g can contribute to torsades.

rows.name: Atropine
rows.dose: 1 mg IV / IO; 2 mg IM reference
rows.watch: Sarin reversal depends on active effect. One reference dose may not reverse exposure.

rows.name: Epinephrine
rows.dose:
1 mg IV / IO; 0.3 mg IM reference
These are NOT push dose amounts.
rows.watch: Push dose action uses mcg. Monitor HR/BP and leakage; excess can trigger AT/SVT.

rows.name: Epinephrine, cardiac vial
rows.dose: Full vial = 1 mg. Mixing 1 mL + 9 mL saline makes 10 mcg/mL.
rows.watch: Do not confuse this with the 1 mg/mL vial: a tenfold concentration difference.

rows.name: Esmolol
rows.use: AFib RVR control; AT / SVT; HR reduction
rows.watch: Premix: 2.5 g / 250 mL, not a bolus. Accumulation can cause bradycardia / hypotension.

rows.name: Lidocaine
rows.use: VT with pulse; VF / pulseless VT support; local anesthesia
rows.dose:
Cardiac: 1 mg/kg = 83 mg at 83 kg
Separate IM/local reference: 100 mg
rows.watch: Shock and esmolol reduce clearance. Toxicity can cause seizures, apnea and arrest.

rows.name: Magnesium sulfate
rows.watch: Reassess rhythm. Excessive delivery rate lowers HR/BP; leaking fluid injures tissue.

rows.name: Norepinephrine
rows.dose:
Model start: 0.05–0.1 mcg/kg/min
At 83 kg: 4.15–8.3 mcg/min
rows.watch: 4 mg is a mixture amount, NOT a patient dose. Assess volume, pressure and line integrity.

rows.name: Calcium chloride
rows.dose:
1 g (10 mL) reference
273 mg elemental calcium
rows.watch: Vesicant. Excess calcium or fast delivery can cause bradycardia, hypotension and arrest.

rows.name: Calcium gluconate
rows.dose:
3 g (30 mL) reference
279 mg elemental calcium
rows.watch: Both salts add to the same calcium burden. Compare elemental amounts; watch the site.

rows.name: Fentanyl
rows.watch: Respiratory depression. Opioids add together; pain relief is not adequate hypnosis.

rows.name: Morphine
rows.watch: Reduced breathing, HR and BP. Poor perfusion reduces IM effect; allow for timing.

rows.name: Ketamine
rows.dose:
Analgesia: 0.2 mg/kg IV or 0.75 mg/kg IM
Induction at full effect: ~1.75 mg/kg IV or 4.375 mg/kg IM
rows.watch: Default induction model, not an instant response. Nystagmus supports sedation assessment; monitor breathing/BP.

rows.name: Midazolam
rows.dose: 5 mg IV / IO; 10 mg IM reference
rows.watch: More may be needed as lidocaine burden rises. Stacking depresses breathing and BP.

rows.name: Propofol
rows.dose: 100 mg reference at 83 kg; scales with weight
rows.watch: No analgesia. Monitor ventilation and BP, especially with opioids or depleted reserve.

rows.name: Rocuronium
rows.watch: Paralysis provides NO sedation or analgesia. Support ventilation; assess hypnosis before and during paralysis.

rows.name: Sugammadex
rows.dose: Binding calibration: 16 mg/kg for up to 1.2 mg/kg available rocuronium
rows.watch: 100 mg is a model unit, not a complete reversal dose. Smaller amounts give proportionate binding capacity.

rows.name: Esketamine
rows.dose: One atomizer = one fixed product dose
rows.watch: Adds to shared sedation. Nausea; combined ketamine-family exposure can depress breathing.

rows.name: Fentanyl lozenge
rows.watch: Patient sitting or lying. Adds opioid burden; monitor breathing and nausea.

rows.name: Penthrox
rows.use: Brief analgesia in an awake patient
rows.dose: One treatment use; reassess before repeating
rows.watch: Repeated uses add exposure. Satisfactory pain relief does not prove ventilation is adequate.

rows.name: Paracetamol / acetaminophen
rows.use: Milder pain with a suitable oral route
rows.watch: Fixed game product units, not an injectable mg reference. Treat the underlying injury.

rows.name: Ammonia inhalant
rows.watch: No extra wake-up roll within 10 s. Correct the cause of unconsciousness.

rows.name: Naloxone
rows.watch: Support breathing. Other sedatives remain active; a new opioid dose can cause renewed effects.

rows.name: Ondansetron
rows.watch: Does not remove aspiration risk, airway obstruction or drug toxicity.

rows.name: Tranexamic acid (TXA)
rows.use: Clot stability; external / internal bleeding control
rows.watch: Continue pressure, dressings, packing and volume treatment. No separate TXA toxicity cutoff is defined here.

rows.name: Ceftriaxone
rows.watch: Uses the ertapenem effect family in the reviewed game data.

rows.name: Ertapenem
rows.watch: No separate drug-specific adverse syndrome in the reviewed path.

rows.name: Hyaluronidase
rows.use: Local rescue for eligible irritant extravasation
rows.dose: 150 units full reference; smaller amounts add within 90 s
rows.watch: For calcium, amiodarone, magnesium, esmolol, HTS or mannitol injury. Use the affected site.

rows.name: Phentolamine
rows.dose: 5 mg full reference; smaller amounts add within 90 s
rows.watch: For epinephrine/norepinephrine injury. Systemic syringe delivery has different effects and can lower BP.

rows.name: Hypertonic saline 3%
rows.watch: Raises sodium; benefit limited by sodium ceiling. Bag and dedicated push effects differ.

rows.name: Mannitol
rows.watch: Adds no sodium, but shares the sodium ceiling gate. Watch local leakage and perfusion.

rows.name: Dimercaprol
rows.watch: UNAVAILABLE. Do not select it as part of a treatment plan.
